description: A deputy general counsel must approve a proposed joint development agreement between the company and Northbridge University and finalize the intellectual-property, grant-compliance, commercialization, and export-control terms, with input from intellectual-property counsel, grants counsel, product counsel, and export counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company and Northbridge University plan to begin a joint battery-inverter research project on July 15.
shared_context.S2: The current draft says that project improvements will be jointly owned, permits publication after a 60-day review, and contains no export-control provision.
shared_context.S3: The draft grants the company a worldwide, nonexclusive license to commercialize project results.
shared_context.S4: Under the legal team's ordinary pre-signature review routine, Elena asks intellectual-property, grants, product, and export counsel to identify any required changes before she approves the agreement.

PF1.text: Thomas reviewed Northbridge University's current invention policy and confirmed that improvements conceived by university personnel must be owned by the university; the company must receive an exclusive commercial license to those improvements rather than joint ownership. He completed this policy check yesterday but has not revised the draft.

PF2.text: Nia confirmed with the university's sponsored-research office that the project uses federal grant funds. The grant requires each subject invention to be disclosed to the government within exactly 60 days after the inventor's disclosure to the university and requires a U.S.-manufacturing preference for products embodying the invention. She received the grant terms this week but has not circulated a compliance schedule.

PF3.text: Daniel documented the company's product team's approved commercialization priority in this week's launch meeting: the license must be exclusive, but only for grid-scale energy-storage systems; the company does not need exclusivity for other fields. The product team recorded this in its launch notes, which have not yet been sent to legal.

PF4.text: Maya classified the project's controlled inverter technology as ECCN 3A001 and confirmed that every transfer of the technical package requires an export-license review before transfer, including transfers to university researchers. She completed the classification review this week but has not added an export clause to the agreement.

acceptance_conditions: Improvements conceived by university personnel must be assigned to the university, with the company receiving an exclusive commercial license.
The exclusive license must be limited to grid-scale energy-storage systems.
Subject inventions must be disclosed to the government within exactly 60 days after inventor disclosure to the university.
The agreement must require a U.S.-manufacturing preference for products embodying federally funded inventions.
Every transfer of the controlled technical package must undergo export-license review before transfer.
The university invention-policy finding must be cited as justification for the ownership and license structure.

content_checks.C2: decisions['commercial_license_type'] == 'exclusive' and any(c['type'] == 'ip_license' and c['target'] == 'company' and c['detail'] == 'exclusive_commercial_license_to_university_owned_improvements' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: decisions['government_disclosure_deadline_days'] == 60 and decisions['us_manufacturing_preference_required'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'grant_compliance' and c['target'] == 'subject_inventions' and c['detail'] == 'government_disclosure_within_60_days_and_us_manufacturing_preference' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: decisions['export_review_required_before_transfer'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'export_control' and c['target'] == 'controlled_technical_package' and c['detail'] == 'export_license_review_before_every_transfer' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft's joint-ownership and nonexclusive-license terms change to university ownership and an exclusive commercial license once the university policy is applied.

The absence of grant information leaves no specific government-disclosure deadline or U.S.-manufacturing requirement, while the federal grant terms impose exactly 60 days and the manufacturing preference.
The draft's worldwide commercialization scope changes to the exact licensed field of grid-scale energy-storage systems once the product team's approved priority is applied.
The draft's missing export provision changes to mandatory export-license review before every transfer once the technology is classified as ECCN 3A001.
